papers.title: Almost-Global Coordinates on Matrix Manifolds
papers.abstract: We study global coordinates on smooth manifolds outside some closed subsets of measure zero. We first give an elementary proof that every compact smooth manifold admits such coordinates, allowing the Euclidean parameter domain to be disconnected. We then study parametrizations of classical matrix groups, Stiefel manifolds, Grassmannians and real flag manifolds. For these parametrizations, we describe the inverse maps and compute the codimensions of the omitted subsets. We construct these parametrizations using Cayley transforms, graphs of linear maps and block Gaussian elimination. We also give formulas for Riemannian gradients and Haar integrals in these coordinates.

papers.title: Round hyperspheres uniquely minimize most tangent-point energies
papers.abstract: We show that round hyperspheres uniquely minimize a broad class of generalized tangent-point energies among all boundaries of bounded Caccioppoli sets sharing the same perimeter or enclosed volume. This includes closed $C^1$-hypersurfaces. Equivalently, we establish sharp lower bounds for the associated scale-invariant ratios of energy to surface measure and energy to volume, respectively, with equality precisely for round spheres.

papers.title: Exotic smooth structures on nonorientable 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct closed nonorientable aspherical 4-manifolds with an arbitrarily large number of distinct smooth structures. This uses the reflection trick of Davis-Hayden-Huang-Ruberman-Sunukjian. Our examples become mutually diffeomorphic after either type of stabilization: taking a product with the real line, or taking a connected sum with sufficiently many copies of S^2 x S^2.

papers.title: Cyclic group actions on K3 surfaces and almost complex structures
papers.abstract: Fintushel, Stern and Sunukjian constructed exotic $\mathbb{Z}_n$-actions on $K3$ for $n=2,3,4$ using twist-rim surgery. We prove that these exotic actions do not preserve any Ricci flat metric or any integrable complex structure. This answers a question of Farb and Looijenga in the negative. In contrast, we prove that any smooth $\mathbb{Z}_n$-action on $K3$ for which the fixed point set has only non-isolated fixed points preserves an almost complex structure with trivial first Chern class. In particular, this applies to the Fintushel-Stern-Sunukjian examples. Lastly, we classify the possible fixed point data and action on cohomology for cyclic group actions on $K3$ of prime order which preserve an almost complex structure with trivial first Chern class.

papers.title: Translation surfaces with logarithmically growing systole
papers.abstract: We exhibit a sequence of translation surfaces $T_1, T_2,...$ with $T_g$ of genus $g$ and area $g$, such that the systole grows logarithmically with $g$. They are produced by starting with a fixed translation surface, taking covers with the same topology as those discovered by Brooks, and then adding handles by gluing along slits.

papers.title: Virtually solvable groups with balanced presentations
papers.abstract: We show that if $G$ is a virtually solvable group with finite Hirsch length and such that $\beta_2(G;\mathbb{Q})\leq\beta=\beta_1(G;\mathbb{Q})$ then $\beta\leq3$. This sharpens bounds on the Betti numbers of 3-manifolds which embed in $S^4$ with the fundamental groups of each complementary region virtually solvable and of finite Hirsch length.

papers.title: Orbifold Morse Handles II. Boundary Regions, Gluing Maps, and Surgery Cobordisms
papers.abstract: We study four-dimensional quotient handles defined by faithful representations of finite groups in $\mathrm{SO}(4)$ and invariant splittings of indices $1$, $2$, and $3$. We identify their attaching and belt regions as oriented $3$-orbifolds described by labeled singular graphs. We determine the orbifold isotopy class of the boundary gluing map. Fix an orientation-reversing orbifold embedding of the attaching region into an oriented $3$-orbifold. Assume that the embedding induces isomorphisms on local groups. The regions, gluing class, and embedding determine the surgery. For a fixed handle and attaching image, an extension condition on the belt region characterizes diffeomorphisms of the cobordisms fixing a specified common exterior pointwise. For index-$2$ handles, this condition is the vanishing of an integer twist in the fixed boundary coordinates. We use these surgeries to construct a compact connected oriented $4$-orbifold cobordism from every closed connected oriented $3$-orbifold $\mathcal O$ to $S^3$. A finite sequence of index-$2$ orbifold handle attachments from $\mathcal O$ to $S^3$ exists if and only if $\mathcal O$ has no tetrahedral, octahedral, or icosahedral vertices. Let $v_{\mathbf T}(\mathcal O)$, $v_{\mathbf O}(\mathcal O)$, and $v_{\mathbf I}(\mathcal O)$ denote the numbers of these vertices. Among finite sequences of handle attachments of indices $1$, $2$, and $3$ from $\mathcal O$ to $S^3$, the minimum total number of index-$1$ and index-$3$ handles is $\left\lceil\frac{v_{\mathbf T}(\mathcal O)}{2}\right\rceil+ \left\lceil\frac{v_{\mathbf O}(\mathcal O)}{2}\right\rceil+ \left\lceil\frac{v_{\mathbf I}(\mathcal O)}{2}\right\rceil$.

papers.title: Positivity of minimal volume entropy for some closed manifolds with zero simplicial volume
papers.abstract: For every integer $m\ge4$, we construct a closed connected oriented smooth $m$-manifold whose simplicial volume is zero and whose minimal volume entropy is positive. This answers negatively the question, attributed to Gromov, whether vanishing simplicial volume implies vanishing minimal volume entropy. Each example has a connected regular five-sheeted covering with zero minimal volume entropy, so vanishing of this invariant does not descend through finite coverings.

papers.title: Branched real projective structures on surfaces, cyclic Higgs Bundles and Anosov representations
papers.abstract: We use the theory of $3$-cyclic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$-Higgs bundles to study real branched projective structures on compact surfaces recently introduced by the authors. After fixing a Riemann surface structure on $S$, the Higgs bundle approach allows us, on the one hand, to construct branched structures with prescribed branching data and, on the other hand, to introduce new classes of such structures. The latter are directly related to singular hyperbolic affine spheres and carry a Blaschke metric with conical singularities. In the final part of the paper, using different methods, we prove that every Anosov surface group representation into $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$ is either Hitchin or belongs to the Barbot component. As a by-product, we obtain that some of the representations associated with the branched structures constructed above are not Anosov.

papers.title: Modular integrals for individual modular knots
papers.abstract: To each modular knot, we attach a weight $2$ modular integral for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ whose homogenized cycle integrals recover its linking numbers with other modular knots in $S^3$. This construction answers Choie-Zagier's question of explicitly constructing modular integrals with given rational period functions in weight $2$. Our formula applies to individual modular knots without symmetrization, thereby realizing an approach discussed but not pursued by Duke-Imamo\={g}lu-T\'{o}th. This gives an answer to Ghys' question on pairwise linking numbers in terms of modular integrals, as sought by Simon.

papers.title: On intersection forms of spin $4$-manifolds with AR homology sphere boundary
papers.abstract: In this paper, building on the work of Dai--Sasahira--Stoffregen, we derive constraints on the intersection forms of smooth, compact, indefinite, spin $4$-manifolds bounded by almost-rational plumbed homology spheres (AR homology spheres) using two methods. First, we use the constraints on the existence of $\operatorname{Pin}(2)$-equivariant maps between representation spheres, established by Hopkins--Lin--Shi--Xu in their proof of the $10/8 + 4$-inequality. Second, we compute Lin's $\kappa o$-invariant for AR homology spheres. Combined with Lin's version of the relative $10/8$-inequality, this computation yields constraints different from those based on Hopkins--Lin--Shi--Xu. As applications, we give an alternative proof of the non-sliceness of the $(2n, 1)$-cables of the figure-eight knot for even $n$---a result originally proved by Kang, Park, and Taniguchi via real Seiberg--Witten theory---by showing within ordinary Seiberg--Witten theory that certain cyclic branched covers of them are nontrivial in the homology cobordism group. We also obtain new lower bounds on the minimal genus of surfaces in various $4$-manifolds bounded by knots whose double branched covers are AR homology spheres. Moreover, we provide an obstruction to smooth $4$-manifold decompositions related to the $11/8$-conjecture.

papers.title: Anosov representations from cyclic Higgs bundles
papers.abstract: For every complex simple Lie group G (not of type $E_8$) we construct the minimal Slodowy slice, which is a half-dimensional slice in the character variety of a closed surface group into G, containing the composition of Fuchsian representations with the minimal representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ in G and invariant under the mapping class group action. This slice is defined via cyclic Higgs bundles, and we show that when G is not of type $E_8$, the corresponding representations are Anosov, so in particular discrete and faithful, and dominate some Fuchsian representation. For each of these Higgs bundles, we consider the equivariant harmonic map to the symmetric space, and we show it is an embedding and a quasi-isometric embedding with regard to the induced metric. From the cyclicity of these Higgs bundles we are also able to construct an auxiliary harmonic map to a pseudoriemannian symmetric space $G/G^\sigma$ which is also an embedding. Our techniques also apply to harmonic Higgs bundles over the unit disk satisfying a certain completeness condition. These techniques also apply to two other families of cyclic Higgs bundles.

papers.title: Link Spectra of Lorenz-like Templates and the Horseshoe
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of the inclusion relations between the link spectrum of the horseshoe template $L(0,1)$ and those of the nonnegative Lorenz-like templates $L(0,a)$. For a template $T$, its link spectrum $\mathscr L(T)$ consists of the link types carried by $T$, allowing parallel strands along its strips. For integers $a\geq0$, the spectra of $L(0,a)$ and $L(0,1)$ are comparable under inclusion if and only if $a\notin\{0,2\}$. More precisely, \[ \mathscr L(L(0,a))=\mathscr L(L(0,1)) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a=1, \] while \[ L(0,a)\prec L(0,1) \qquad (a\geq3). \] For $a=0$ and $a=2$, the two spectra are incomparable. The main new containment is \[ L(0,2n)\preceq L(0,1)\qquad(n\geq2), \] which goes beyond the classical parity-preserving nesting relations. A key ingredient is a braid-theoretic criterion: every $T$-link \[ T((r_1,s_1),\ldots,(r_k,s_k)) \] with $s_k\geq2r_k$ is a horseshoe link. This gives a large explicit family belonging to both the Lorenz and horseshoe spectra. In the reverse direction, we construct a horseshoe link which is not Lorenz, thereby disproving the Birman--Kofman conjecture that every horseshoe link is a Lorenz link. For each integer $m\geq6$, we obtain infinitely many horseshoe links of braid index $m$ excluded from every other nonnegative $L(0,a)$. These examples give infinitely many links with any prescribed number of components at least three. In the other direction, for each positive number of components, we give infinitely many links carried by both $L(0,0)$ and $L(0,2)$ and excluded from the horseshoe spectrum.
